headline: Approved zoning relief at 41 Linden, 97 Boston, and 7 Skerry streets; continued three other petitions to November 18.
summary: Four petitions were approved, including a special permit for a rear addition at 7 Skerry Street. Three others were continued to November 18, 2026, for plan changes or additional relief.
decisions: Approved a special permit for a single-story rear kitchen addition and rear deck at 41 Linden Street, 4-0.
Approved a variance and special permit to convert vacant commercial space at 97 Boston Street to residential units, 4-0, with a recommendation to convert unused parking to outdoor space.
Continued the variance request for a 1.5-story addition and landing at 8 1/2 Rear Allen Street to November 18, 2026, 4-0.
Continued the variance request for an elevated deck and staircase at 19 Bertuccio Avenue to November 18, 2026, 4-0.
Approved a special permit for an 11-foot-tall rear addition at 7 Skerry Street, 4-0, with a condition to move two master bedroom windows.
Continued the variances and special permit for two accessory dwelling units at 111 Mason Street to November 18th, 2026, 4-0.
Approved a six-month extension of rights granted for 55 Butler Street U2, 4-0.

City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
DRAFT Meeting Minutes 
October 14, 2026 
 
A special meeting of the Salem Zoning Board of Appeals (“Salem ZBA”) was held on Wednesday, 
September 9, 2026, at 6:30 pm via remote participation in accordance with Section 30A of Chapter 
20 of the Acts of 2021, as amended by Section 40 of Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2023, and further 
amended by Section 1 of Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2025, the City is authorized to conduct remote 
meetings of its public bodies through June 30, 2027.  
 
Acting Chair Christa McGaha calls the meeting to order at 6:30 pm. 
Acting Chair McGaha explains how individuals can participate in the meeting remotely via Zoom, 
and that instructions to participate remotely can also be found on the Salem website.  Ms. McGaha 
also explains the rules regarding public comment. 
 
ROLL CALL  
Those present were: Vice Chair Christa McGaha, Peter Habib, Hilary Forbes, and Samantha 
Stringfellow.  Also in attendance was Brennan Postich — Staff Planner.  Those absent were: Chair 
Nina Vyedin, Secretary Ellen Simpson, and Stephen Larrick. 
 
REGULAR AGENDA   
Location: 41 Linden Street (Map 33, Lot 0380) (R2 Zoning District) 
Applicant: Martin J. Schneer 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of MARTIN J. SCHNEER 
at 41 LINDEN STREET (Map 33, Lot 0380) (R2 Zoning District) for a Special 
Permit per Section 3.3.5 Nonconforming Single- and Two-Family Residences of the 
Salem Zoning Ordinance to construct a single-story rear kitchen addition and a rear 
deck, with a seven-foot side setback and an eight-foot rear setback, to a 
nonconforming two-family structure. 
 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha introduces the petition.  
 
Attorney Joseph Dever introduces himself on behalf of the petitioners and discusses the property at 
41-43 Linden Street while presenting a plot plan and dimensional table.  The two-family residence 
was constructed in approximately 1900.  Mr. Dever discusses the existing and proposed conditions 
resulting from the proposed addition.  He also notes existing nonconformities.  Mr. Dever describes 
the enclosure of the existing porch and the proposed deck.  Mr. Dever discusses the dimensional 
table and setbacks, as well as the relief being requested.  He contends that the proposal is not any 
more detrimental to the neighborhood.  Mr. Dever also indicates that some neighbors have rear

decks similar to what is being proposed and asserts that it is in line with neighborhood 
characteristics.  Mr. Dever presents elevations showing existing and proposed conditions and asks 
that the Board grant the requested special permit. 
 
Mr. Habib asks clarifying questions about the dimensional table, asking if the deck should be 
included in the setback and lot coverage calculations.  Mr. Dever states that he would be happy to 
submit a revised table if required.  The Board discusses that matter and asks to see the architectural 
plans to determine that the rear deck is not covered.  Ms. McGaha states the lack of additional roof 
area allows the Board to interpret the petition as such that a revision is not required. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha opens the floor to public comment, but there is none.  Ms. McGaha also 
discusses the special permit criteria.  The Board discusses and finds that the petition meets the 
criteria. 
 
Motion and Vote: Mr. Habib motions to approve the petition of MARTIN J. SCHNEER at 41 
LINDEN STREET (Map 33, Lot 0380) (R2 Zoning District) for a Special Permit per Section 3.3.5 
Nonconforming Single- and Two-Family Residences of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to construct a 
single-story rear kitchen addition and a rear deck, with a seven-foot side setback and an eight-foot 
rear setback, to a nonconforming two-family structure, subject to the following standard conditions: 
1. Petitioner shall comply with all city and state statutes, ordinances, codes, and regulations. 
2. All construction shall be done as per the plans and dimensions submitted to and 
approved by the Building Commissioner. 
3. All requirements of the Salem Fire Department relative to smoke and fire safety shall be 
strictly adhered to. 
4. Petitioner shall obtain a building permit prior to beginning any construction. 
5. The exterior finishes of new construction shall be in harmony with the existing structure. 
6. A Certificate of Inspection is to be obtained 
7. A Certificate of Occupancy is to be obtained 
8. Petitioner is to obtain approval from any City Board or Commission having jurisdiction 
including, but not limited to, the Planning Board. 
9. Unless this Decision expressly provides otherwise, any zoning relief granted does not 
empower or authorize the Petitioner to demolish or reconstruct the structure(s) located 
on the subject property to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its floor area or 
more than fifty percent (50%) of its replacement cost at the time of destruction.  If the 
structure is demolished by any means to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its 
replacement cost or more than fifty percent (50%) of its floor area at the time of 
destruction, it shall not be reconstructed except in conformity with the provisions of the 
Ordinance. 
10. All construction shall be done per the plans and dimensions submitted to and approved 
by this Board.  Any modification to the plans and dimensions must be approved by the 
Board of Appeals unless such changes are deemed a minor field change by the Building 
Commissioner in consultation with the Chair of the Board of Appeals. 
11. Petitioner shall schedule Assessing Department inspections of the property, at least 
annually, to project completion and a final inspection upon project completion.

Ms. Stringfellow seconds the motion.  The vote is four (4) in favor (Peter Habib, Christa 
McGaha, Hilary Forbes, and Samantha Stringfellow) and none (0) opposed.  The motion 
passes. 
 
   
Location: 97 Boston Street (Map 15, Lot 0217) (R2 Zoning District) 
Applicant: De Sieu Lam 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of DE SIEU LAM at 97 
BOSTON STREET (Map 15, Lot 0217) (R2 Zoning District) for a Variance per 
Section 3.2.2 Home Occupations of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to change a vacant 
first-floor commercial space to two residential units, and a second-floor commercial 
spa to one residential unit, without changing the structure’s footprint, creating a lot 
area per dwelling unit of approximately 2,582 square feet where 7,500 square feet per 
dwelling unit is required. 
 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha introduces the petition.   
 
Attorney Shutzer introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner.  He notes the four-member Board 
and asks if it would be permissible to continue the matter if, after discussions, it seems like having a 
fifth-member vote would be helpful.  Chair McGaha states the petitioner can request to continue at 
any point.  Mr. Shutzer describes the property at 97 Boston Street and explains that it is currently 
used for commercial purposes, further noting that a petition was previously approved by the Board 
to operate a pet grooming business.  Pursuant to difficulties renting the space and concerns raised by 
neighbors that the business was not appropriate for the location, the petitioner now wishes to use 
the space for residential purposes, which Mr. Shutzer indicates is consistent with the need for 
additional housing.  Mr. Shutzer describes the relief being requested to change the commercial use 
on the first floor to two units and the second floor to a third unit, where each would be 
approximately 1,300 square feet.  Mr. Shutzer notes a large parking area in the rear.  Mr. Shutzer 
presents a plot plan and asks the Board to approve the relief associated with the transition of the use 
and the lot area per dwelling.  Floor plans are shown demonstrating proposed conditions. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha notes that it may be more appropriate to seek relief of a variance per section 
4.1.1 and a special permit per section 3.3.2 to change from one nonconforming use to a less 
detrimental nonconforming use, rather than the relief being sought under section 3.2.2.  She also 
notes that the matter would not need to be re-advertised because the description of the proposal is 
accurate and the relief itself is of the same magnitude, just more appropriately under a different 
section.  Mr. Shutzer agrees.   
 
The Board discusses the petition and relief being sought.  Ms. Forbes asks about the second mode 
of egress for the upstairs unit.  Mr. Habib asks about the excess of five parking spaces and if there

space depending on how many spaces the Board would like.  Mr. Lam states he would be amenable

actually no requirements for parking based on the zoning here, and that there may be a benefit to 
reducing the number of spaces.   
 
Acting Chair McGaha opens the floor to public comment, but there is none. 
 
The Board discusses the petition and relief being sought, as well as the benefits of additional 
housing in a residential district.  They also discussed the parking area and special conditions 
regarding hardscaping and greenscaping.  The Board suggests that any unused parking spaces be 
converted into green space.

2. All construction shall be done as per the plans and dimensions submitted to and 
approved by the Building Commissioner. 
3. All requirements of the Salem Fire Department relative to smoke and fire safety shall be 
strictly adhered to. 
4. Petitioner shall obtain a building permit prior to beginning any construction. 
5. The exterior finishes of new construction shall be in harmony with the existing structure. 
6. A Certificate of Inspection is to be obtained 
7. A Certificate of Occupancy is to be obtained 
8. Petitioner is to obtain approval from any City Board or Commission having jurisdiction 
including, but not limited to, the Planning Board. 
9. Petitioner shall obtain street numbering from the City of Salem Assessor’s Office and 
shall display said number so as to be visible from the street. 
10. Unless this Decision expressly provides otherwise, any zoning relief granted does not 
empower or authorize the Petitioner to demolish or reconstruct the structure(s) located 
on the subject property to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its floor area or 
more than fifty percent (50%) of its replacement cost at the time of destruction.  If the 
structure is demolished by any means to an extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its 
replacement cost or more than fifty percent (50%) of its floor area at the time of 
destruction, it shall not be reconstructed except in conformity with the provisions of the 
Ordinance. 
11. All construction shall be done per the plans and dimensions submitted to and approved 
by this Board.  Any modification to the plans and dimensions must be approved by the 
Board of Appeals unless such changes are deemed a minor field change by the Building 
Commissioner in consultation with the Chair of the Board of Appeals. 
12. Petitioner shall schedule Assessing Department inspections of the property, at least 
annually, to project completion and a final inspection upon project completion.

And the following special condition: 
  1. The Board recommends that the petitioner convert any unused parking areas to usable  
       outdoor space for the three dwelling units, such as greenspace or hardscape in lieu of  
       asphalt parking. 
 
Mr. Habib seconds the motion.  The vote is four (4) in favor (Peter Habib, Hilary Forbes, 
Samantha Stringfellow, and Christa McGaha) and none (0) opposed.  The motion passes. 
 
   
Location: 8 1/2 Rear Allen Street (Map 41, Lot 0159) (R2 Zoning District) 
Applicant: Lacey Smith 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of LACEY SMITH at 8 1/2 
REAR ALLEN STREET (Map 41, Lot 0159) (R2 Zoning District; Coastal Resiliency 
Overlay District) for a Variance per Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements of the 
Salem Zoning Ordinance to extend a nonconforming single-family house by 
constructing a 1.5-story addition and landing to the house’s north and east sides. The 
proposed addition would have a five-foot side (north) setback and be located inside the 
required side (south) setback, and the landing would have a one-foot side (north) 
setback. The property’s lot coverage would increase from 23% to 44%, where 35% is 
permitted. 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha introduces the petition.  
 
Isaak Estrada of SL Haus Group introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner.  Mr. Estrada 
describes the relief being sought and states the petitioner seeks improvements related to accessibility 
on the first floor for the family’s care of their daughter and to accommodate caretakers.  Mr. Estrada 
presents a plot plan demonstrating existing and proposed conditions, as well as floor plans showing 
existing and proposed conditions.  He speaks to the desire to make the family more comfortable and 
discusses various elements such as the proposed ramp and landing, and maximizing the space for 
accessibility.  Mr. Estrada states that the petitioner is open to Board feedback and changing requests 
in order to make this project work as well. 
 
Ms. Smith introduces herself and describes her family and their needs, noting that she has a 15-year-
old daughter with a rare genetic condition that requires extra care and assistance.  Ms. Smith 
indicates that for the last 15 years she has had to carry her daughter up and down the stairs to her 
bedroom, and that the proposal is focused on keeping the family in their home with accessibility 
improvements.  She adds that currently there is not enough space to store her daughter’s wheelchair 
and that it is stored in the car overnight. 
 
Elevations showing existing and proposed conditions are presented, and Mr. Estrada describes the 
proposed changes further and the project goals.
City of Salem Zoning Board of Appeals 
October 14, 2026 DRAFT Meeting Minutes

Mr. Habib asks clarifying questions regarding parking, and Mr. Estrada explains that the existing 
shed would be removed and provides additional clarification regarding potential available parking.  
The existing right-of-way is also discussed.  Ms. McGaha notes that the Board would like to see 
where the parking would go in the plans, and whether there would be any encroachment on the 
shared easement.  The height and roof are discussed, as well as the number of stories.  Mr. Habib 
notes that there needs to be a change to the proposed eave and slope; otherwise, the petitioner will 
also seek an additional variance for the number of stories.  Ms. McGaha asks about potential 
changes to the ramp and expresses concerns about parking. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha opens the floor to public comment. 
 
Diane Savickas of 8 Allen Street, Units 1 and 2, introduces herself as an abutter and states that the 
plot plan she has is different from the one submitted by the petitioner.  Ms. Savickas states that the 
building identified in the petitioner’s plan as a garage is actually a three-bedroom residence.  She also 
expresses concerns about clearance, proximity/density, and risks of fire.  Ms. Savickas also suggests 
there is a tree that is not currently shown in the petitioner’s plans, and questions how a ramp and the 
parking will all fit with the additions.  She also expresses concerns about water runoff and snow 
removal, and states she does not think this is an appropriate project. 
 
Cynthia Pappas of 8 Allen Street, #3 introduces herself and states she resides in the building that has 
been misidentified in the petitioner’s plot as a garage.  Ms. Pappas states there is an emergency 
egress behind her home that connects numbers 6, 8, and 8 1/2.  Ms. Pappas states she understands 
the family’s needs and would like to be supportive as much as possible but has concerns about 
spacing.  She also expresses concerns about snow removal, venting, and density.  She suggests there 
must be some kind of compromise that keeps safety for all in mind. 
 
The Board discusses needing an updated plot plan and identification of any paving and existing 
trees.  They also suggest getting feedback from the fire department on the fire egresses, as well as 
any relevant legal advice. 
 
The petitioner asks to continue the petition to the next regularly scheduled meeting to provide plan 
changes and updates. 
 
Motion and Vote: Mr. Habib motions to continue the petition of LACEY SMITH at 8 1/2 REAR 
ALLEN STREET (Map 41, Lot 0159) (R2 Zoning District; Coastal Resiliency Overlay District) for 
a Variance per Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to extend a 
nonconforming single-family house by constructing a 1.5-story addition and landing to the house’s 
north and east sides to the next regularly scheduled meeting of the Zoning Board of Appeals on 
November 18, 2026. 
 
Ms. Stringfellow seconds the motion.  The vote is four (4) in favor (Christa McGaha, Peter 
Habib, Hilary Forbes, and Samantha Stringfellow) and none (0) opposed.  The motion 
passes.

Location: 19 Bertuccio Avenue (Map 24, Lot 0098) (R1 Zoning District) 
Applicant: Jordan Sidebottom 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of JORDAN SIDEBOTTOM at 
19 BERTUCCIO AVENUE (Map 24, Lot 0098) (R1 Zoning District) for a Variance per 
Section 4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to construct an 
approximately twenty-foot-tall elevated deck and a 9.5-foot-tall staircase to the front of a 
nonconforming single-family house. The proposed deck would have a six-foot side 
setback and an eight-foot front setback. The proposed staircase would extend 
approximately eight feet from the elevated deck to the front property line. 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation 
 
Acting Chair McGaha introduces the petition. 
 
Isaak Estrada introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner and describes the proposed deck 
extension.  Mr. Estrada notes the existing deck that led to a landing which has been demoed, and an 
existing garage for which access will be maintained.  Mr. Estrada presents a plot plan showing 
existing and proposed conditions and discusses the proposed deck and steps.  Mr. Estrada presents a 
demo plan and scope of work, as well as elevations showing existing and proposed conditions. 
 
The Board members ask clarifying questions and discuss lot coverage, noting that the dimensional 
table would need to be updated to reflect the lot area of all the roofed areas.  Mr. Habib states he 
does not love or understand the proposed roof above the deck.  He also questions whether the 
extension fits in the neighborhood.  Mr. Estrada explains the roof design further.  Ms. McGaha 
states that the petitioner will need the additional relief of a variance for lot coverage and a special 
permit for nonconforming structures. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha opens the floor to public comment, but there is none. 
 
The Board discusses the petitioner further and asks additional questions regarding whether there 
were alternatives considered that would not go up to the lot line in front.  Mr. Estrada expresses a 
willingness to adjust the deck and stair dimensions to provide some setback.  The Board discusses 
whether to require plan revisions or special conditions.  They also review and discuss the 
dimensional table and need to update it. 
 
The petitioner requests to continue to the next regularly scheduled meeting to provide plan 
revisions. 
 
Motion and Vote: Ms. Forbes motions to continue the petition of JORDAN SIDEBOTTOM at 
19 BERTUCCIO AVENUE (Map 24, Lot 0098) (R1 Zoning District) for a Variance per Section 
4.1.1 Dimensional Requirements of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to construct an approximately 
twenty-foot-tall elevated deck and a 9.5-foot-tall staircase to the front of a nonconforming single-
family house to the next regularly scheduled meeting on November 18, 2026.

Location: 7 Skerry Street (Map 36, Lot 0138) (R2 Zoning District) 
Applicant: Stacey J. Pappas 
Project: A public hearing for all persons interested in the petition of STACEY J. PAPPAS at 7 
SKERRY STREET (Map 36, Lot 0138) (R2 Zoning District) for a Special Permit per 
Section 3.3.5 Nonconforming Single- and Two-Family Residences of the Salem Zoning 
Ordinance to construct an approximately eleven-foot-tall, 38.5-foot-long single-story 
rear addition to a nonconforming single-family house. The proposed addition would be 
located 4.5 feet from the side (west) property line. 
 
 
 
Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha introduces the petition. 
 
Attorney Bill Quinn introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner.  Darguin Fortuna and Whandy 
Martinez also introduce themselves as project architects.  Mr. Quinn explains that the petitioners are 
aging and have been residing in their home for 15 years, with the house in the family since the 
1950’s.  He describes the property and states that the rooms are too small for the occupants, with 
steep and narrow stairs and hallways.  Mr. Quinn also discusses other hardships that have resulted in 
the petitioners seeking to create an addition to the rear of the house to provide a main bedroom and 
bath so they can shift most of their living to the first floor.  He also discussed the relief being 
requested. 
 
Mr. Martinez discusses the design of the proposed addition as well as the functional purposes of the 
addition to improve accessibility and allow the residents to age in place.  He presents a map of the 
area as well as a plot plan showing existing and proposed conditions.  Floor plans are also shown, as 
well as elevations showing both existing and proposed conditions. 
 
The Board members ask clarifying questions regarding the plot plan and setbacks.  Mr. Habib asks if 
the petitioner would be open to removing some of the windows in the new master bedroom for 
privacy reasons. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha opens the floor to public comment, but there is none. 
 
The Board continues to discuss the matter as well as a potential special condition regarding the 
windows being discussed for removal.  The petitioner notes that there are no structures, just yard 
and fence where the proposed windows would face.  Mr. Habib suggests a condition would still be 
good for privacy reasons.  Mr. Quinn indicates the abutting neighbor has not mentioned being

Documents and Exhibitions     
 Application date-stamped ______, 2026 and supporting documentation. 
 
Acting Chair McGaha introduces the petition. 
 
Attorney Ryan Carlucci introduces himself on behalf of the petitioner and explains that the 
petitioner came before the Board in August and received approval to make a rear addition to the 
existing building to turn a one-family dwelling into a two-family dwelling.  Mr. Carlucci explains that 
the proposal is now to add two ADU’s on the lot and in the existing garage.  He discusses the relief 
being sought and the ADU requirements per the Salem zoning ordinance.  Mr. Carlucci notes the 
proposed second curb cut for a total of 36 feet where 20 feet is required, and that a Special Permit is 
required for the second ADU. 
 
Ms. Forbes asks if the proposed ADU’s are in addition to the previously permitted addition, and Mr. 
Carlucci states that is correct.  Ms. Forbes asks about the impact on utilities, and Mr. Carlucci 
suggests they will be minimal.  She also confirms that there would be long-term rentals.  Mr. Habib 
asks about parking, and Mr. Carlucci provides clarifications.  They discuss the parking further, and 
Mr. Habib expresses concerns regarding the speed with which people travel on this street and the 
curvature of the road with respect to the second curb cut.  Mr. Habib also expresses concerns about 
density and accessibility for the rear-most proposed ADU in the event of an emergency.  Ms. 
Stringfellow also expresses concerns regarding safety related to parking and the road conditions.  
The Board states it would be good to get feedback from the fire department regarding emergency 
access.  Ms. McGaha notes that the previous Board decision from August had a special condition 
that said the plans would be revised to remove certain parking spaces.  Ms. Stringfellow asks about 
the choice of basement and ground floor units rather than above ground units.  Mr. Carlucci states 
the petitioner did not want to build up unnecessarily.  A plot plan and elevations are presented 
showing existing and proposed conditions.  Mr. Habib asks about drainage, and Ms. Stringfellow 
states she would also like feedback from an engineer regarding drainage impacts.  The Board asks 
about lot coverage as well.
